body.heading: Chapter 1: The cat who watched the sea
paragraphs: On a tiny island of grey rock, in the middle of a wide blue harbour, stood a lighthouse painted in stripes of plum and gold. At the top of the lighthouse lived Keeper Ada, who tended the great lamp. And at the bottom, in a basket by the warm stove, lived Mango — a small orange cat with a white chest, stripes on his back, and a tiny brass bell that went tink, tink, tink wherever he went.

Mango knew the lighthouse the way you know your own home. He knew all one hundred and twelve steps up to the lamp room — he had counted them, slowly, the winter he was a kitten. He knew which step creaked, which window the gulls liked best, and exactly where the sun fell for his afternoon nap. But most of all, Mango knew the boats.

Every evening, when the sky turned the colour of peach jam, Mango climbed to his favourite flat rock and watched the harbour come home. There went the green fishing boat, chugging in heavy with the day's catch. There went the ferry, bright and busy, carrying people to the town across the water. And there, smallest of all, went a little blue sailing boat with one white sail, no bigger than a teacup from Mango's rock. Mango did not know whose boat it was. He only knew it always came home last — and that its tiny light always twinkled back at the lighthouse, as if to say: I see you. I'm safe.

body.heading: Stop and think
paragraphs: Before you read on, think: Mango watches for the little blue boat every single evening. What do you think he would do if one evening the boat did not come home?

body.heading: The evening the boat didn't come
paragraphs: Then, one October evening, the wind came up rough and the waves stood tall and white at the top. Mango climbed to his rock and watched, whiskers blowing. The fishing boat came home. The ferry came home. But the sky grew dark, and darker still — and the little blue boat did not come.

Mango's ears went up. His tail went still. Somewhere out in that dark, wild water was a tiny boat with one white sail. And just then, high above him, the great lamp made a small, strange sound — sputter, sputter — like a candle in a draught. Mango stared up at the tower, his heart thumping. If the lamp went out, who would show the little boat the way home? Find out in Chapter 2.

body.heading: Words to know
paragraphs: Harbour — a safe place by the sea where boats shelter from rough water.
Keeper — a person whose job is to look after something, like a lighthouse.
Sputter — to make small popping sounds, as if about to stop.
Draught — a current of air moving through a room or doorway.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Why do you think Mango watches for the little blue boat every evening, even though he doesn't know whose it is?
2. What do you think Mango will do next — and what in the story makes you think so?
